text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm updating the rerank endpoint contract. Two sticking points: request idempotency (replays) and deterministic tie-breaking across clients/models. Want to lock behaviour before API review.
vikram: For idempotency are we expecting clients to pass a request_id? or should we derive one server-side from payload?
maria: prefer client-supplied request_id for dedupe, optional. If absent, server can still attempt a best-effort canonicalization but must not promise exact dedupe guarantees.
josh: +1 for explicit request_id. Also: if request_id used in tie-breaker hash, replays get the same ordering which seems good. But we need to document that in contract.
kelly: how about backward compatibility: older clients may not set request_id; ordering should remain deterministic even without it. Maybe use candidate_id as fallback tie key.
maria: design proposal: primary sort by score (desc), then stable tie-break using: if request_id provided -> hash(candidate_id + request_id), else -> hash(candidate_id + model_version). This keeps old clients stable.
vikram: can we show small pseudocode in contract? e.g.
```
if score_a != score_b: return score_b - score_a
else:
  seed = request_id or model_version
  return compare(hash(id_a + seed), hash(id_b + seed))
```
josh: looks good. Need to call out: hash must be specified (e.g., xxhash64) and endianness so implementations in other langs match. Also define seed concatenation format to avoid collisions (use `id + ':' + seed`).
maria: agreed — contract will specify using xxhash64(id + ':' + seed) as uint64, compare numerically. Add example.
kelly: question on score semantics: should score be a float between 0-1 or arbitrary model score? Consumers assume higher==better. We should be explicit.
maria: keep it generic: "score: number, higher is better" and add optional normalized_score (0..1) for clients that want it. Document preferred field names: `score` (required), `normalized_score` (optional).
sre-bot: deploybot: FYI deploy of rerank-v2 schema validator in staging at 1956790000.
josh: also need to define behavior for null/missing scores: treat as -inf (sorted last) and stable tie-break applied among nulls too. Call out that we don't want to crash.
maria: will add: "missing or null -> treated as -Infinity, preserved with deterministic tie-hash."
vikram: what about rounding/precision? If services do float32 vs float64 they might produce equalish ties. Maybe document tolerance: ties are exact equality on the provided numeric value — no epsilon. If callers want robust ties, they should supply normalized_score with agreed precision.
maria: ok: "equality defined by bitwise equality of transmitted numeric representation; no server-side epsilon." We'll call out recommended practice.
kelly: final: API change policy: adding new optional fields allowed; removing or renaming `score` not allowed. Schema version bump only for breaking changes.
maria: thanks. I'll draft the contract text and include the pseudocode + example request/response and push to the API PR. Ping me if you want edit rights. :thumbsup:
josh: quick nit — include an example curl and a sample response with tie ordering deterministic.
maria: will do. I'll update the PR today and mention xxhash impl refs. If no objections, will ship to docs tomorrow.
vikram: no objections from me.
kelly: approved from infra side.
sre-bot: ack: noted on staging validator run.
